Cyber Attack Disrupts Ecuador’s Construction Materials Industry: Holcim Ecuador SA Among Victims

A cyber attack believed to be ransomware has crippled the IT systems of key construction materials firms in Ecuador, with Holcim Ecuador SA confirming it is among those affected. The attack, which began late Tuesday evening, has interrupted business operations across multiple companies, causing delays in the delivery of cement, aggregates, and related products to construction projects nationwide.

According to a statement released by Holcim Ecuador SA this morning, the company’s digital platforms, including order processing and inventory management systems, were rendered inoperable after unauthorized access was detected. “We are working closely with cybersecurity experts and authorities to restore our services as soon as possible,” the statement read, emphasizing that customer data protection remains a top priority.

Other firms, including Cementos Andinos Ltda. and ConstruMat S.A., have also reported technical disruptions, though details remain limited as investigations continue. Industry analysts warn that the attack could have significant ramifications for the sector. “Construction projects rely on just-in-time delivery. Even a few days of disruption can delay projects and increase costs,” said María Fernanda Zambrano, a consultant specializing in industrial supply chains.

The National Union of Construction Workers of Ecuador expressed concern over potential knock-on effects. “If material deliveries are stalled, there is a risk of temporary work stoppages on sites,” said union spokesperson Jorge Paredes.

The Ecuadorian Chamber of Construction Materials Suppliers called on authorities to prioritize the investigation and to support affected businesses. “Our industry is vital for ongoing infrastructure and housing projects,” said the Chamber’s president in a brief statement.

As of Wednesday afternoon, cybersecurity teams were still working to assess the scope and origin of the attack. There is no official estimate yet as to when normal operations might resume.
